name: Minimum-impedance measuring relay
summary: Measuring relay that compares voltage with current and operates when the apparent impedance falls below a set value.
description: A minimum-impedance relay divides measured voltage by measured current and operates when the result falls below its setting, indicating a fault close enough to fall inside its reach. It is used as generator and transformer backup protection and is the basic idea behind distance protection.

The relay needs both CT and VT inputs, so the symbol should always be read with both connections. It does not show the characteristic shape on the impedance plane, any directional element, or the loss-of-voltage blocking needed to avoid operation when the VT supply fails.
readingNotes: Confirm both voltage and current inputs are shown.
distinction: A minimum-impedance relay uses voltage and current together; an overcurrent relay uses current alone.
